notes.title: Narrative Designer on Trailblazers - Devlog #04
notes.notes: [p]Hey Trailblazers, it’s yer boi, yer gal, yer narrative designer Jen.[/p][p]I come from the land of comics but have been entranced by video games from the first time saw the manhole cover explode in Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles. Video games were prohibitively expensive for a divorced family and I rarely asked for new games, the Game Boy was revolutionary because it could travel with me. My sixth birthday was in a New York arcade, back when arcades existed. Kids had two hours to play all the games they wanted, except the claw machine, pizza and cake, and then the birthday kid got to play the claw machine until they won something. I would host the same party today for my friends.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/a59f6dc6b0a8026cc4c055b00930e28e0cdb9133.jpg"][/img][/p][p][i]Jen as the villain in an annual dinner theater production at the University of Texas at Austin called Madrigal Dinner.[/i][/p][p]Now there are games at the library or mediatheques, which I know a younger version of me would have loved. Games can be rented for free or played at some libraries, they are included in streaming apps. But the library was my main home and best friend as we moved (every summer) until high school. We moved so much that the first place we visited once moved in was the library so I could get a card and my mom would ‘give permission’ for me to check out books from any section (many libraries let kids check out anything, as they should, but my mom wanted to make sure it was noted in my file).[/p][p]Not to be ‘that person’ but I read everything, or try to. I always try to have one non-fiction book going along with fiction because in there lies the keys to so many new stories. But I’m also a sucker for horror, science fiction, fantasy, and mystery. The unknown revealing itself calls to me. From reading Shirley Jackson’s [i]We Have Always Lived Here[/i], to scaring myself in Vermont with Stephen King’s [i]IT[/i], to pledging my fealty to [i]Gideon the Ninth[/i] by Tamsyn Muir to traveling Gethen in [i]The Left Hand of Darkness[/i] by Ursula K. LeGuin to attending Oozma University in the [i]Binti[/i] by Nnedi Orkorafor.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/0e4b4bb62e4a4ebaca58dbf823bc0b4868cb2012.png"][/img][/p][p][i]Covers for Gideon the Ninth, The Left Hand of Darkness, and the Binti collection.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]When I was high school, I went to a romance/fantasy reading group run by my best friend’s mom, we would often get free copies of books from publishers in exchange for feedback, writing honest reviews, and to with help word of mouth. I was soon able to decipher the rhythm of romance, it’s a nice comfort genre but the thrill of science fiction, the different magic systems of fantasy, and the hoping to hell the hero makes it through in horror or finding the murderer have a bigger draw as they are the things I am least likely to grasp within my lifetime.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/47cdbbbb673115b31cd4f16ab4c51ae093f38c1a.jpg"][/img][/p][p][i]Screenshot of Where in the World is Carmen Sandiego? (1995)[/i][/p][p][/p][p]These were same genres I’m attracted to in video games! The exquisite glory of [i]Where in the World is Carmen Sandiego[/i] on PC, which I replayed recently, as a way to encourage people to use the included encyclopedia was a giant bridge for reader like me to get into games more. As a kid, the definitive ending of each mystery, racing against my own brain, felt perfect.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/58ea593793d35e91e5eb2a543e2aad0ccffdb443.jpg"][/img][/p][p][i]One of the boss fights in Paper Mario: Origami King. With clear blue skies.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Now, what often what draws me into a video game is the color palette: limited or moody, evoking a feeling. So many games use every color and it’s not in service to the story. If the mood of the game was a color or the easy pairing of like colors vs the jarring dissonance of complimentary colors, what would it be? How can you revisit this prismatic thesis? Maybe I’m an art snob, or it relates to comic book printing (my full work background is in comics) but I will play an okay board game with gorgeous art, but I have to be bribed with cheese to play an ugly looking board game with great mechanics. Case in point: [i]Paper Mario: Origami King[/i]—absolutely loved that game, it was fantastic and scratched all those itches but boss fights fought in the bright sunlight are so wild to me. Being color palette-inclusive, I just made up this phrase, is a way to appeal to wider audiences I suspect. But, damn, put out a game only in coral pink, navy, and teal—I’m wishlisting it.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/34edc53fc1c8ec12a74d297c5d397c6e138f010a.jpg"][/img][/p][p][i]Still from the movie adaptation (2018) of Annihilation (2014), featuring plants growing into the forms of humans in conversation.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]I joined the Strangers team in late 2024, and it was clear they loved [i]Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind[/i], [i]Howl’s Moving Castle[/i], and [i]Rimworld[/i]. Luckily, I had read, watched, and played most of the influences the team agreed on and began to work in my own world-building as well. Some of my big influences for Trailblazers are the Southern Reach Trilogy by Jeff Vandermeer ([i]Annihilation, Authority, Acceptance,[/i] the first of which was made into a movie); [i]Ingress[/i], Niantic’s firstish geolocation game, and the [i]Past is Red[/i] by Catherynne M. Valente.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/fcf4e2ad857d1d648b0e2a59020c2e22a706f896.png"][/img][/p][p][i]Logos for two podcasts; the first is of The Magnus Archives, the second is The White Vault.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]With some dashes of [i]The X-Files[/i], [i]Control,[/i] and the [url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SCP_Foundation"][u]SCP Foundation[/u][/url] (thanks to Arnaud Gattlen for introducing me to this), and the travelogues of real world explorers and expeditioners who met their doom. As a cartoonist who listens to a lot of audiobooks and podcasts, the collection aspect of stories like [i]The Magnus Archives[/i] and found ephemera like [i]The White Vault[/i] definitely seeps into the March as well. One of the biggest themes these worlds have in common is the environment itself is a character. Which means, it can change, it can grow, it can be hurt, and it can harm.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/ee67d0185ae3c8d53e08a5d678fb02fea25713c1.jpg"][/img][/p][p][i]Screenshot from Control (2019) featuring main character, Jesse Faden, staring at some floating employees of the FBC, Federal Bureau of Control.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]The body horror and evershifting landscape met with the beaurocratic-military urge to control it is never not funny and fascinating to me, as seen in the Southern Reach trilogy in Area X, the same for the AWEs in [i]Control[/i]. It feels like a Western world theme, domination and power over the elements, instead of learning to live with them. This is the biggest choice you must make in [i]Ingress[/i], there are alien elements invading the world via Exotic Matter on the map, and you can choose to Evolve with it (as the Enlighted team) or Fight back against it (as the Resistance). The way Ingress folded diegetic audio elements in with their game play, so as you walked closer to an area dominated by one of the two factions the ambient audio changed, honestly blew me away. This wasn’t uncommon in video games, but this in an ARG (augmented reality game), I was playing on my phone and walking in my neighborhood. I wouldn’t play the game if I forgot my headphones or (later) hadn’t charged them, it felt crucial for immersion in the game.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/4c5af71843bc2700e8b9e9f1e33124686c4d4dc1.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][i]The cover of The Past is Red, A panel from Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind by Hayao Miyazaki, and the symbols for the two original factions from Ingress.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]It’s that same rhythm, or more like under-the-skin-tapping I felt reading [i]The Past Is Red[/i], where the main character lives in an apocalyptic world of rising waters and everyone lives on trash islands, munching on their favorite microplastics with hints of real food. The rise of Funko Pops, custom dice, acrylic standees, keychains, all the many plastics that I encounter at conventions is the baseline for this possible future author Catherynne M. Valente penned so clearly. In this book, it is very much the people who are 100% to blame for their current situation. In Trailblazers, a science-fantasy, there’s a bit more to it than just our own hubris.[/p][p]So yeah, do I think Trailblazers are literary people? Abso-f**king-lutely. However, they rose from the ashes and had to rebuild libraries and write new masterpieces as well as beach reads. Cunning Trailblazers might have found a book from the Time Before out in the March, secreted it away, and rewrote it as if it were their own writing. Assuming, of course, that book was GOOD.[/p][p]“[i]May I present to you Selene Netherland’s Bram Stoker’s Dracula. Wait, dammit.”[/i][/p][p]Some Trailblazers still have stories from the past passed down via oral traditions, or via drawings. In a future devlog, I’ll talk about the different factions and their lore! The story we are most excited for, of course, is the one you make in the game.[/p][p]I hope you liked what was essentially a prose version of a slideshow of “stuff I like and want to write within the same vibe.” I’m sure you want to hear more about the lore of the factions or March next time, so let me know in the comments or if you have any questions![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/96a1cb18fc7a7d69119e992b4e6861e648850c44.png"][/img][/p][p][i]Books on the floor in the Trailblazers game.[/i][/p][p]Jen[/p]

notes.title: Portrait Procedural Generation - Devlog #03
notes.notes:
[p]Hello, I’m Adrien Cantone, Art Director for [i]Trailblazers: Into the March[/i], and this is my first devlog for the game! Today, I’m going to talk about how we created the assets used to generate the thousands of crew members you’ll be taking care of in the game! Before that, a few words about myself for those who might be interested.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Who am I?[/b][/h2][p]I’m a French artist in my twenties who studied illustration and comic books. I quickly realized that comics weren’t my dream job and that I preferred video games and animation. Back then, there weren’t many schools in France for this, so I taught myself using online resources from artists such as Alexandre Diboine, Marco Bucci, Gop Gap, Tim McBurnie, and many more![/p][p]So if this is a career you want to pursue, there’s no need to pay for expensive schooling—you can find everything you need online! My first jobs were with animation studios such as Amopix and Sony Pictures Animation. Then, after a few freelance gigs as a concept artist for video games, I ended up at Strangers![/p][p]During the job interview with them, I had very little information about the game, but I was already inspired by the concept. I came in with a vision for the graphic style I wanted to bring to [i]Trailblazers[/i]. I had just discovered the amazing work of Calum Alexander Watt and showed it to the Strangers team as one of my inspirations. They loved the direction! Over time, we added many more references and inspirations to the moodboard, and if I had to summarize them, it would look something like the image below.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/059f7c2c010dbef046ee1e4a191ab79248d0c4a2.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Crew members[/b][/h2][p]For this first devlog, I think it would be interesting to talk about the procedural generation of portraits. In [i]Trailblazers[/i], you can recruit randomly generated crew members at the Hub. You can see their portraits, but you’ll also see them on the ship in a simplified look we call “[i]Pawns[/i]”! Creating the art for [i]Trailblazers[/i] presented me with numerous challenges. As an artist, this is by far the most complex project I’ve ever worked on, for a few reasons:[/p][list][*][p]The top-down camera view (it’s hard to make things both readable and visually appealing from above).[/p][/*][*][p]The need to generate thousands of unique crew members.[/p][/*][*][p]The fact that we’re a small indie team (I’m the only full-time artist on the project!).[/p][/*][/list][p]I’ll show you the workflow we used to create the crew members despite these constraints![/p][p][/p][h2][b]Pawns[/b][/h2][p]Pawns are the main way characters are represented. This is how crew members appear on the ship and on excursions. It’s a simplified, almost abstract view that still gives the player an understanding of their movements and designs, even at a distance or awkward camera angles.[/p][p]To create all the assets efficiently, I took inspiration from Lego and divided the assets like this >>

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/68c90b589444e8d8bd8c6cfa514f604b919a16dc.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The advantages of this approach:[/p][list][*][p]All characters can share the same animations for arms and legs regardless of body shape.[/p][/*][*][p]Not all animations need to be hand-made—the head can be programmed in Unity to turn towards objects, making characters more expressive.[/p][/*][*][p]Characters can easily equip objects and share the same gear, enhancing customization and player attachment.[/p][/*][*][p]Specificity: most assets—like face, hair, arms, and legs—exist in horizontal versions for when the character sleeps, faints, or dies. (It’s a lot of work!)[/p][/*][*][p]It’s not in the game yet, but I dream of characters evolving physically over time based on what they experience—like losing a limb or gaining weight.[/p][/*][/list][p]Including animation frames, we currently have 540 assets for the pawns, and we’ll have even more as we add gear and tools.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/4505eec096fcb442d80374616bbac58fb67c18e6.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2][b]Portraits[/b][/h2][p]A face is the first element through which a player connects emotionally to a character. That’s why pawns aren’t the only visual representation of your crew. We built a portrait generator that uses just a few layers to create thousands of expressive, semi-realistic faces.[/p][p]It’s made of 13 layers, in this order:[/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth="77,"][tr][td colwidth="77"][p]1[/p][/td][th][p]Hair Underlay[/p][/th][/tr][tr][td colwidth="77"][p]2[/p][/td][th][p]Face[/p][/th][/tr][tr][td colwidth="77"][p]3[/p][/td][th][p]Wrinkles[/p][/th][/tr][tr][td colwidth="77"][p]4[/p][/td][th][p]Earrings[/p][/th][/tr][tr][td colwidth="77"][p]5[/p][/td][th][p]Face Paintings[/p][/th][/tr][tr][td colwidth="77"][p]6[/p][/td][th][p]Cyber Modifications[/p][/th][/tr][tr][td colwidth="77"][p]7[/p][/td][th][p]Mouth[/p][/th][/tr][tr][td colwidth="77"][p]8[/p][/td][th][p]Nose[/p][/th][/tr][tr][td colwidth="77"][p]9[/p][/td][th][p]Eyes[/p][/th][/tr][tr][td colwidth="77"][p]10[/p][/td][th][p]Eyebrows[/p][/th][/tr][tr][td colwidth="77"][p]11[/p][/td][th][p]Suits[/p][/th][/tr][tr][td colwidth="77"][p]12[/p][/td][th][p]Beard[/p][/th][/tr][tr][td colwidth="77"][p]13[/p][/td][th][p]Hair Overlay[/p][/th][/tr][tr][td colwidth="77"][p]14[/p][/td][th][p]Equipment[/p][/th][/tr][/table][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/1645e9ff4bfa0d543c3a13c36f94d4eed63f052f.gif"][/img][i]Example of how the layers assemble to create a face[/i][/p][p][/p][p]We currently have 500 hand drawn assets in this portrait generator. These portraits play a very important role in making each character generated by the game unique and i hope it will increase the emotional connection between the player and their crew members.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/5c02e30cc0562374c64410debcfd334d88cbc527.gif"][/img][/p][p]As you can see, a cat has sneaked into the portraits: your crew won’t be limited to humans. Animal and robotic companions can join your adventures too. They perform simple but useful tasks—cats chase rats that steal food, while robots carry heavy resources. Their portraits and pawns are simpler than humans’, with only color variations within each type.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/c59214178a9aa057de39b757da2e26a44bd02d85.gif"][/img][/p][p]One of our next task is to to adjust the parameters of our portraits generator to visually showcase the different factions in the game. Here is an early test of that with the Scavengers faction ! Only they will be able to have that equipment and tattoos on their portraits.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/b712417ac2c7acf82f720bb2ca4090a5808af291.gif"][/img][/p][p]I hope you liked this first Art devlog, please let me know if there is a specific topic you want to learn more about next time ! Bye ![/p][p]Adrien[/p]

notes.title: Trailblazers team at Gamescom
notes.notes: [p]Dear Trailblazers,[/p][p]This post is to announce that part of our team is currently at Gamescom, Cologne, Germany, World, Solar System, Milky Way galaxy. For those who are there and want to come say hello and test the demo with Arnaud (Game Director), Jen (Narrative Designer) or Alyssa (Creative Designer), the team is at the Joystick Ventures booth ([b]hall 10.2, booth E043G[/b]).[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/070bf6a05cbd32f15f732ae317314029401aa849.jpg"][/img][/p][p]As you can see, the mood is great![/p][p]Vincent[/p]

notes.title: 🏆 Winner at ChinaJoy + Trailblazers Joins Tiny Teams 2025!
notes.notes: [p]We’ve got incredible news to share — Trailblazers: Into the March just won [b]Best Visual[/b] at [b]Game Connection x JoyChina 2025[/b], part of ChinaJoy, one of Asia’s biggest game industry events! Being recognized as the winner in visual direction is a huge honor. We’ve poured our hearts into crafting a world that feels both strange and beautiful, and it means so much to see that work celebrated on an international stage. Adrien is the hand behind these creations, and if you join us at Gamescom, you’ll potentially get to meet him IRL! Below is a sketch of our first landship, with its final version evolving as we go along, and a sketch of the Yoke. The team will tell you more about it in an upcoming post.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/164586700b0c8aff525f80dc64a9a268f2aace10.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/8e2efe42947a7d92ec291a23eb77d45a506883c3.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/70a3cd5a59955f5d2829d110104b59420daaad5f.jpg"][/img][/p][p]But that’s not all…[/p][p][/p][p]Trailblazers has also been selected to take part in [b]Tiny Teams 2025,[/b] the amazing indie game showcase hosted by Yogscast Games! Tiny teams can create big worlds — and we’re proud to be one of them. This showcase highlights games built by small, passionate teams, and we’re honored to be included alongside so many brilliant indie projects. We can’t wait to show off more of the March during the event.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you for supporting us on this journey. Being part of these events — and winning awards — wouldn’t be possible without your encouragement and feedback. Stay tuned… more is coming soon![/p][p][/p][p]— The Strangers Game Studio team[/p]

notes.title: Welcome to the March - Devlog #02
notes.notes: [p]Hey there, Strangers from the Internet! I hope you’re doing all right![/p][p]I’m Arn, game director on [i]Trailblazers: Into the March[/i] and this my first devlog.[/p][p]Have you ever wondered what the world might look like a thousand years after humanity nearly wiped itself out in an orgiastic cataclysm? Fantasized about what kind of explorer you would’ve been when the world was still wild and wide? Spent sleepless nights thinking, “Isn’t it [i]Into the Marsh[/i]? Did they make a typo in their title? Should I be worried for them?”[/p][p]Well fret not, benevolent reader, as I’m here to answer some of those questions.[/p][p]As the title says…[/p][p][/p][h1]Welcome to the March[/h1][p]Firstly, let’s clear the air: It’s [b]March[/b], not [b]Marsh[/b]. Unbeknownst to some people with a richer social life than me, a March describes a borderland territory and was used during Medieval European times to qualify all kind of contested land, untamed regions or buffer zones between different states. In our case the best variation of this word comes from the Old Norse word [b]mǫrk,[/b] meaning “forest, woodland, borderland”.[/p][p]We choose this word for two reasons:[/p][olist][*][p]We thought it was a well-known word.[/p][/*][*][p]It described exactly what we wanted our game world to be.[/p][/*][/olist][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/91c725765427bfbe7c3b3ae07f016dd2cbb602d9.png"][/img][i]Here is a fun fact: In WoW, the French translation of “Westfall” is “La Marche de l’Ouest”. Which means Westmarch. It has absolutely nothing to do with our game. But I don’t see another time in my life where I’ll get to share this, so I’m taking the shot.[/i][/p][p][/p][h2]From phantasmagoric sea to ever-shifting lands[/h2][p]As you might know [i]Trailblazers: Into the March[/i] started as a project about pirates. The pitch we decided, as a crew, to develop was “FTL X Pirates”. So the first iterations of the March were actually iterations of the “8th Sea”:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/5894f8c0a688d2f17ab7d392f0bdda352aa47915.jpg"][/img][i]Players were supposed to navigate the 8th Sea, a sea of phantasms and magical realism.[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/a05f1757487b65d05a014554bd9e35b2bae9f761.jpg"][/img][i]We weren’t sure of the 3D vs 2D direction yet so were looking to make it interesting in top-down view also.[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/e3ccb7cf0a52fa9c0dd6f489f65437ebc9614aeb.jpg"][/img][i]I just like this one so I’m showing it to you. Shout out to @[b]arnowillustrations [/b]who was working as an artist on the project back then.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]The fundamentals were very close to what we have today though:[/p][list][*][p]The player would leave a main port to explore an uncharted area at the fringe between reality and the supernatural.[/p][/*][*][p]Expeditions were prepared in the port. Player had to manage their resource stock, choose a hull and loadout, pick crew members, and venture forth to fulfill contracts.[/p][/*][*][p]The sea was everchanging by nature. We kept that idea with the March.[/p][/*][/list][p]When we decided to commit fully to our 2D top-down perspective and transitioned to the idea of Landships we looked for a way to maintain the core premises we liked with the Pirate fantasy : the crew, the port, the uncharted and living unknown to explore.[/p][p]We found inspiration in many places, but the most essential ones were :[/p][list][*][p][i]Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind[/i] (and generally speaking Hayao Miyazaki’s work as a whole)[/p][/*][*][p][i]Stalker[/i], be it the film from Andrei Tarkovski or the games from GSC Game World[/p][/*][*][p][i]La Horde du Contrevent[/i], a French science-fiction novel by Alain Damasio[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h2]Nausicaa: Voracious toxic jungle[/h2][p][i][b]Nausicaä[/b][/i] is a post-post-apocalyptic world, a bit like [i]Horizon: Zero Dawn[/i], [i]Zelda: BotW[/i], or ours <3.[/p][p]It means the story takes place long after the world as we know it has ended. The cataclysm is far away in the past, and civilization now endures or rebuilds within a transformed world.[/p][p]In [i]Nausicaä[/i], humanity survives in scattered pockets, struggling against the ever-spreading, hostile spore-forest known as the “Rotten Sea.” From a human perspective things are quite desperate, between stagnation and warring states reproducing past mistakes.[/p][p]The March in [i]Trailblazers[/i] draws directly from this. Humanity is confined to a fragile enclave, any expansion endeavor being blocked by the March. Political tensions are rising between the different nations of the enclave, a path through the March must be found.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/d42a90a7a9ec08d069f1fe9e3401bf33059e8001.png"][/img][i]A guy lost in the Rotten Sea. If you want to delve in Nausicaa because it piqued your interest know that the film is good but the manga covers more ground and is even cooler.[/i][/p][p][/p][h2]STALKER: Journey through the Zone[/h2][p]In [i]STALKER,[/i] a group known as the Stalkers are specialized in venturing into the “Zone”, a surnatural area surrounding Chernobyl. They serve as guides, mercenaries or simply go there to scavenge valuable artifacts created by the Zone.[/p][p]At the center of the Zone lies a Monolith who can supposedly grants one’s heart true desire. The film and the game series have different tonalities but they both tell the stories of people seeking to reach the heart of a dangerous and unpredictable region in search of meaning, redemption, or something they can’t name.[/p][p]The Trailblazers are inspired by the Stalkers. And at the center of the March lies something that calls to those willing to reach it.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/a46157039337f2fd9d696d8a630ecfc7fb87ab07.png"][/img][i]In S.T.A.L.K.E.R: Shadow of Chernobyl you can meet other Stalkers on your journey. This games really succeed in creating a feeling of diffuse community with those characters. Translating this in Trailblazers is a dream of mine.[/i][/p][p][/p][h2]La Horde du Contrevent: Expedition 34[/h2][p]In [i]La Horde du Contrevent[/i], humanity survives in a world ravaged by violent winds. We follow the 34th "Horde” a group of 23 individuals trained from birth to go against the wind and discover its origin. They leave the bastion of humanity to go and explore their world to secure the survival of civilization.[/p][p]In [i]Trailblazers: Into the March[/i] we took the consecutive expeditions trying to go further and further, leaving from the last city before the March: Terminas.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/ddf667f816adcd69b822f6648ae31a172d021590.png"][/img][i]La Horde du Contrevent got a French comic book adaptation. There was also a game project crowdfunded back in the days but I think it might have been abandoned. At least we got Expedition 33 to fill that hole in our heart so we got that going for us![/i][/p][p][/p][h1]Shaping the March[/h1][p]With enough inspirations to guide us it was time to give shape to the March. We wanted it to have different type of biomes so we started to do some moodboard research to pinpoint what we were looking for exactly.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/83c9baecca4d3eec9e256222d4254bd7ac2aa854.jpg"][/img][i]A glimpse on an early internal moodboard. I’m only showing a sample of it as we want to keep some surprise.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]We decided to start with the biome that would feel the more “vanilla” but that would also solve some challenges like level of depths and strong variations. We went to develop what we call internally the [b]\[Untamed Forest][/b].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/e857aea3c849719c6749f39044b565b5a8e7c06a.jpg"][/img][i]Those were some initial top-down asset sketches to build the biome.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]In parallel we worked on the general lore and structure of the game. We did some research on the general March map, but also on the actual city of Terminas.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/95c549b30edaf33cf20265653bd26cf5b08ca3aa.jpg"][/img][i]Research made for the overworld map structuration.[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/8f19bb188797ad23f3dd2a17302649729dfecbb5.png"][/img][i]Concept sketch made by Adrien on the city of Terminas, from which every expedition into the March starts.[/i][/p][p][/p][h2]Looking for gameplay expression[/h2][p]While the art team (of one) was working on defining the vibe of our universe, the rest of the team was looking to find a way to express our fantasy into gameplay. And let me tell you, benevolent reader, the relationship between the March, the landship and movement in our game has been the subject of many iterations.[/p][p]Before we settled on this more constrained “corridor” design we had tested a lot of different solutions :[/p][list][*][p]Early on, you could roam freely on the map and send your characters outside of the landship to cut some trees. Your landship could even shoot at poop-throwing monkeys, giant frogs and weird caterpillar creatures (I’ll show them to you one day).[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/fb93ac5d4daa52c3920b88c518aa27978ca0e864.gif"][/img][i]We were using a placeholder for the landship back then, thank you @scribblesinspace. We never met nor talked but I used this ship of yours in super early mockups of the game.[/i][/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="X13EQ5Zr4wk;full"][/previewyoutube][list][*][p]As we advanced towards a combat structure based on tactical duels between landships, we rebooted the way movement worked in the game and tried to have a more constrained structure, closer to classical roguelite design, with simple lines and points.[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/215a6af0782c010c3b972874e1b4788e0f00a753.png"][/img][i]At a certain point, the whole Journey was reduced to a gauge progressing beneath the landship screen and the March maw was chasing you, forcing you to advance.[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/845f670b0304785e7454acc9ace02c604d288b3c.jpg"][/img][i]In this version Player could travel to different points and events would unfold as text-based adventures.[/i][/p][list][*][p]Different iterations followed, with the intent to make things less abstract and to bring back the free-roaming. We tested a lot of things. Each of those iterations ended up defining what we have today one way or another.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/cc8d3791fa2e34f01ea68a59224b96fdf1de247d.jpg"][/img][i]At a certain point we were pondering making the map low-poly and look a bit like Zelda: Link’s Awakening.[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/e504e9909567f42d696aa9e88d463393095ad37e.gif"][/img][/p][p][i]The idea of having a sonar was there quite early in the project. While I dug for references I stumbled upon Barotrauma and was mesmerized by their sonar system.[/i][/p][p][/p][list][*][p]Finally, the split between the two parts came. The structure solidified with an [b]overworld map[/b], called the \[March Map]. This map has nodes you’re going to explore in a more direct way, called \[Journeys] for now. Those moments compose the main part of the gameplay loop. We’ve been mainly focusing on \[Journeys] since then to make sure this part of the loop is functional and cool to play.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/278edaa5178464119c778072a9b2ac83305067a2.jpg"][/img][i]The March Map and the nodes you’re going to explore[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/d3a41329eb56a73bdc59c45ced1c8bb7876de985.png"][/img][i]One of the research mockups for the Journey map coupled to the landship advancing in its corridor.[/i][/p][p][/p][h1]Of March and Men[/h1][quote][p]In [i]Trailblazers[/i], the world has ended, and from its ruins, a new one rose. Humanity has reached its natural border: the March. If civilization is to endure, a path must be opened. A trail must be blazed. You are a Trailblazer, the captain of a Landship: a roving refuge shaped by necessity and daring hearts. Your lifeline in this hostile region. You have been charged with a mission: uncover the secrets of the March and discover what lies at its core.[/p][/quote][p]This devlog was meant to give you insights on what we’re creating and how the process goes behind the curtain. It’s a fascinating endeavor to build a world, especially one who’s meant to be played. To be fully transparent with you, benevolent reader, I think it’s a bit magical and I’m not always sure of how things happens. It’s a collective effort influenced by all kind of conflicting needs, desires and unpredictable parameters.[/p][p]As the poet says : [i]“The best laid plans of March and Men often go awry”[/i][/p][p]But constraints in art tend to generate the coolest things.[/p][p]I’m really proud of being part of this team and of the work we’re doing. All the people involved went from turning this mockup:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/826909566e5a9767712063da39422bae9da17b3d.jpg"][/img][i]This one was made with DnD battlemap resources I could find online.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Into those wondrous interactive paintings, with living characters in it. Dreaming, like we all do, of eating a good meal or taking a nap :[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/8e2efe42947a7d92ec291a23eb77d45a506883c3.gif"][/img][i]I didn’t touch on sub-biomes variations subject. But the Untamed Forest already have a bunch of them, it might be a topic to adress in a future devlog![/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/311f3a8032a9b11c74353aa90b90a13ceca1a231.gif"][/img][i]This one is currently my favorite biome I think. I’m not sure I should say that? The mix of coral and fungal aesthetic with the slow spore rain makes me want to live there (with a gas mask).[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/8a2651cdd8cce56077a70de73e430aec69cd107f.gif"][/img][i]Our art team has been hard a work to create cool landmarks to discover in those biomes and we can’t wait to show them to you.[/i][/p][p][/p][p]Voilà.[/p][p]I hope you enjoyed the read, if you’re still here you have all my gratitude. Let us know what you thought of the format, we always appreciate feedbacks on form or substance. We have ideas for the next devlog but if you’re curious about things feel free to ask![/p][p]Take care of yourself Trailblazers,[/p][p]and see you in the March.[/p][p]Arn[/p]

notes.title: We have successfully completed our first-ever external playtest!
notes.notes:
Hello, Trailblazers!
For the past month and a half we've been hard at work cooking our very first playtest ever! We wanted to share the process with us, and of course, talk about the future! So grab a cozy drink, sit down, and let's get to the issue!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/bcf3f899549f50240c82c4aceca8ac82be94e305.png[/img]

[h2]Setting the bases for the first public playtest[/h2]
Developing a game takes a lot of iteration, a lot of coming and going, and a lot of rethinking things. Weaving player opinion into this process is a surefire way to elevate the game to greater heights! At Strangers, we were certain [b]we want to involve the players in the development process[/b], and have been doing so since the early times of Trailblazers: Into the March, but it was time to take a way more direct approach by [b]letting people actually play[/b] a bit of our game [b]for the first time[/b]!

To that end, we devised a first external playtest [b]focused on the combat[/b] in the game. We prepared a build that included some battles, one boss battle and a secret boss after beating all the base ones! We made sure the build was stable, and that it included enough content so that players could get a good idea of what playing Trailblazers combat would feel like. Of course, these builds are super early work, so they will be improved upon tirelessly, and the final version might be very different!
                                       
We prepared a very complete [b]initiation document[/b] walking players-to-be through the basic game mechanics, the game controls, the weapons that would be available, some hints on combat, and the very essential [b]feedback survey[/b] we kindly asked them to fill in after playing!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/334e835d22315491cce8a2ff18d3eda654ff0ae6.png[/img]

[h2]Choosing the playtesters![/h2]
Long before the playtest started, we had already been crafting a list of playtesters. Because the game [b]is still in the early stages of development[/b], and since this was our [b]first foray into playtesting[/b], this first playtest was [b]comprised mostly of our family and friends[/b]. We also included some longtime members of the Discord community, and after a few days, we also gave the chance to random players in our Discord server, and members of the FTL subreddit who would be familiar with the mechanics and feel of Trailblazers.

Since this was our first time doing an external playtest, the [b]outreach process was organic[/b] and a little bit clunky! We contacted every one of the participants manually, processed their NDA individually and handed each of them a unique key. We want to take this chance to apologize deeply if we have accidentally missed someone in this storm of mails, sorry! We have learned from this and are [b]looking into ways to automatize and improve this process[/b] so we can focus entirely on your feedback and on working on the game instead of being forced to spend the day in e-mail turn-based combat.

We would like to, of course, [b]continue expanding our list of playtesters[/b]! New eyes can see new things, and the more eyes we have on the game the better our chances to identify and address issues and problems. That said, we're a teeny tiny team, so we have to [b]keep the numbers manageable[/b] with our current forces, and we might have to alter some aspects of the playtests, like the way we collect feedback. We hope you'll understand! We will always do our best to listen to all your feedback, though, promise!


[h2]What we learned[/h2]
We asked playtesters to [b]fill in a form after playing[/b] so they could give us their feedback and opinion on a set of specific questions. Out of the 65 people who received a key to try the game, [b]41 players answered the survey[/b], and we're endlessly grateful to those who did! We thoroughly read all the feedback provided, and we arranged them form replies neatly in a set of analytical graphics so we could really take in the data. We have more than 10 hours of player footage from our playtester, and we’ve sat through it like one does with a good movie!

We'd love to make an entire [b]post on the analytics[/b] of this first playtest in the future, but for the time being we can tell you that most people enjoyed the combat, and many found the game to be just the right difficulty or even a bit too easy! We also learned the UI is not necessarily easy to take in for all players: with the UI being front and center in games, we're making changes and adjustments to it immediately, in hopes for the next playtest it'll be clearer and easier to comprehend for everyone!

We also discovered the most liked enemy Landship by the playestesters was [b]the Urchin[/b]! Congratulations to our favorite Landship of the month, even if as an enemy!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/d99051baf64c10aa26f4fdd096cb99dd286ac8c1.jpg[/img]

Most of the playtesters were really in agreement that the art was great, and our hearts are warmed by your positive feelings towards it!

We got a lot of clear indicators and actionable pointers on ways the combat can be improved, and so we'll be working hard to make the most out of your precious opinions to make Landship combat as great and fun as can be!

[h2]Future playtests?[/h2]
If you've gotten this far, this is your reward: [b]yes, our dears! There will be more public playtests in the future[/b] and we'd be happy to hear from more people, our existing playtesters and new ones! Since we're still refining our ways and processing this one, [b]we're not able at the time to provide a date for the next one[/b], but we'll make sure to reach out to more people once we're ready for it! It's a good idea to follow us on [url=https://linktr.ee/trailblazers.game]our social media[/url], and also to stay tuned [url=Discord.gg/Trailblazers]to our Discord server[/url]! We will also make sure to post here, but you know us devs tend to naturally inhabit Discord servers.

Future playtests might iterate over features that have already been playtested, like combat, or might cover different features and game mechanics. It's still early to promise you anything, Trailblazers, but rest assured you'll have more chances to provide direct feedback, test the game and help us in its creation in the future!

[h2]Closing words[/h2]
[b]We want to thank all our playtesters[/b] for the precious time they took to play Trailblazers: Into the March and provide us with excellent feedback! We also want to thank all the people who asked to be part of the Playtest and couldn't make it this time: we're sorry, we'll do our best to include you in the future!
[b]Thank you as well to our loving community[/b], who support us and cheer us on everyday! Let's all keep working to make Trailblazers: Into the March the greatest game ever!

Until then, see you soon, Trailblazers. Stay vigilant in The March.

notes.title: Devlog #001 - We are Strangers
notes.notes:
You might know us, you might not. Some of you frequently ask about updates on Trailblazers : Into the March. Where does this game come from? What kind of crazy people launched a new video game? My name is Vincent, co-leader of this madness! And I'm here to tell you about us. Game On.

[h1]Turning a Reddit Post into a Company[/h1]
Trailblazers is born from a new team and company. It all started from a [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/INAT/comments/v2gxgc/lets_dream_together/]Reddit Post[/url] I wrote in 2023 asking to find crazy peers to do a game. The post didn't mention any specific game idea or genre; it was more focused on the idea of creating a company and choosing a project together.

In retrospect, it was probably a good idea. It allowed us to find a better idea than I would have found on my own, and it immediately ignited passions within the team. What are we going to do? We decided to pitch ideas internally. About thirty projects were proposed, and the debate was heated to decide what we were going to do.

While most in the team had already worked in the video game industry, we had never worked together. Personally, I trained as a film-maker and art historian, and my first passion is music. So I wasn't necessarily prepared to do something in the video game industry. But when you're passionate about art, technology and storytelling, video games are an infinite playground that you can invest in. And it's possible to create all of this with just a computer. It's magical! I fell in love. 

Being an entirely remote company, we decided to call ourselves Strangers. The year 2023 and a large part of 2024 were therefore devoted to setting up a game project, a team, a business project, networking, meeting publishers, attending fairs - and all this with very limited financial means. A lot of stress, a lot of work and a lot of passion. As you've probably noticed, we have now signed with Joystick Ventures and this partnership allows us to work under good conditions and focus on the Trailblazers Universe.

[h1]Are the pirates gone?[/h1]
Trailblazers was born from a simple idea by Vlad, our lead developer and co-founder of Strangers (yeah, yeah, I know, he's the one who won the internal pitch...). 

“Let's take FTL, but instead of a spaceship, let's put pirates on a ship.”

Okay.

But where's the ship in Trailblazers? And the pirates?... They no longer exist… Yes… I know, dear pirate lover… they no longer exists… It's a fact we'll have to live with. 

We were keen to create a rich and complex world and we thought that pirates were already laden with stereotypes, with strong imagery carried by cinema and video games. We wanted a more neutral playground. So we invented the Trailblazers and their landships. We borrowed certain mechanics from our pirate prototype and the desire to create a community simulation, transformed the ship into a landship and the pirates into Trailblazers. 

[i]Quick tip: To transform a ship into a landship, you simply take the word ship and add the prefix land in front of it - easy.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/afa0a196f6aa08229f60069252824749d2f92b54.png[/img]
[i]Image of Crow’s Nest prototype. A project we sank.[/i]

[h1]In Love with Landships[/h1]
Can you be obsessed with Landships? Why not, I don't see how that's any different from being obsessed with a pair of shoes. This love for landships materialized through the work of two artists who helped us make these vessels tangible, several prototypes, attempts to make them move with elegance in Unity, and many other wild projections. It's not so different from boats after all (apart from the wind, the water, the flotation point, the rotation inertia, the XXX, the YYY, and so on).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/5b6ef901a9b6304e1c5058b94c269f21b9138625.jpg[/img]

[i]Concept art by Clément, with whom we worked at the start of the project.[/i]

[h1]The gameplay[/h1]
Arn, our game designer, will talk to you more extensively about the gameplay soon, but I can already give you two or three indications. The game unfolds across two distinct parts: Terminas, which is the main HUB, and the March. In the HUB, players can purchase and customize their landships, recruit crew members with unique origins, traits, skills, trade supplies and materials, and undertake contracts for the March. In the March, players manage their crew's daily lives, witness their evolving relationships and stories, engage in tactical Landship battles, explore uncharted territories, and respond to a variety of dynamic events and challenges.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/5bec04d0a9a52f8e37ca31e4dc361509e09835d4.png[/img]
[i]The hub, the March and a landship[/i]

[h1]What are we doing now?[/h1]
While I'm writing this post, people on the team are actually working - on the Landship Life and Combat Systems. As you likely know, these two elements will be essential parts of Trailblazers.

Life on the ship is certainly what will make Trailblazers so special - but from a game design perspective, it's also the most complicated part. We are working with certain influences - Rimworld, Oxygen Not Included, The Sims - but we simply cannot replicate community life by flatly copying these games. It is necessary to arrive at a unique solution that is in total harmony with what it means to be a Trailblazer on a Landship.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/0bc2d70e5dfa90469273727817e4ac32a624421c.png[/img]
[i]The guy with the tree leaf[/i]

We're trying to model human lives, with all their complexity, biases, etc. And often, the most human-like behaviour comes from bugs or elements that haven't been fine-tuned yet. Look at this character, for example, who never wanted to leave his tree leaf. He grabbed it and kept it for hours. Absolutely unplanned - but I find it very beautiful.

These kinds of little moments also guide us in the development of this Landship Life. This appears to us as a surprise, but it's a good surprise, it's human behaviour. So I don't know if this character will still have his leaf when you play Trailblazers, but I hope so for his sake, he seems quite attached to it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45048165/6c5468e0602be54e3ce1c952a5596beb145403ba.png[/img]
[i]If you think we should keep it, you’re not alone.[/i]

We will share new elements soon, so stay tuned dear Trailblazers! In the meantime, if you wish to learn more about the game and be a member of its community, join us on [url=https://discord.gg/r4wwcEggkp]Discord[/url], follow us and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2671300/Trailblazers_Into_the_March/]wishlist the game[/url].

Thank you for your attention,

Vincent, from the Strangers team
